public_rationale: Both parts hold. A CNBC report quotes Burry saying that extending useful lives to understate depreciation "artificially boosts earnings," so that was his stated reason. The same report states the GAAP mechanism: a longer estimated life lowers the yearly depreciation expense that hits the bottom line. Real cases match. Alphabet's move to six-year server lives cut 2023 depreciation by $3.9 billion and raised net income by $3.0 billion. Analysts also found that Microsoft, Amazon and Oracle's extensions raised net income. Whether longer lives are realistic is a separate question. The claim here is only that spreading costs out makes reported profits look better, and the evidence shows it does.
limitations: Company figures come from press and analyst reports because SEC pages were blocked.
Not every firm moved in the same direction at every point; the claim is about the mechanism, not every firm's latest change.
